newsitem.title: USA: USAir engine failure being investigated - FAA.
newsitem.headline: USAir engine failure being investigated - FAA.

text.p: The FAA said Thursday it continues to investigate an engine failure that canceled a USAir Group Inc flight earlier this week.

There were no injuries and the incident was what the FAA terms "self-contained," meaning that debris was blown out the back of the rear-fuselage-mounted engine as it was designed to do in such a mishap, FAA spokeswoman Kathy Higgins said.
USAir said the engine was replaced and the McDonnell Douglas Corp MD-80 airplane is back in service.

Flight 2250, bound from Cleveland to Charlotte, N.C., left the gate Monday but as the pilot powered up to take off, the mishap occurred, a USAir spokesman said. The plane taxied back to the gate and passengers were put on other flights, he said.

He said the airplane had two Pratt & Whitney JT8D-217 engines, which are in the JT8D-200 series but a different model than one that exploded last summer, killing two when debris flew sideways into a Delta Air Lines Inc airplane in Pensacola, Fla.
Pratt & Whitney is a unit of United Technologies Corp. Boeing Co plans to acquire McDonnell Douglas in a stock deal.
